managed_cloud.note: AGI Managed Cloud's own retention: conversations are kept until the user deletes them or the account, with no automatic expiry enforced today; temporary chats expire in about 30 days by a daily job (https://agiworkforce.com/privacy). There is no mode where AGI itself stores nothing: the workspace zero-data-retention setting controls which upstream model providers a request may route to, not AGI's own storage of the conversation. Training commitment is at https://agiworkforce.com/terms section 05: AGI does not train AGI-owned models on submitted content, explicitly not a promise about a third-party model provider's handling. Data is hosted in the United States only; AGI does not offer EU or UK data residency (https://agiworkforce.com/privacy#s-08).

openai.note: Abuse-monitoring logs are held up to 30 days unless the law requires longer. Zero data retention needs prior approval and drops the request from those logs. Regional processing covers the United States, the European Economic Area with Switzerland, and the United Arab Emirates; the other listed regions are storage only.

anthropic.note: API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days of receipt, with exceptions for the Files API, custom agreements, usage-policy enforcement and legal holds. Zero data retention exists as a separate agreement. No residency region list is published.

google.note: On the paid tier Google does not use prompts, cached content, files or responses to improve its products. Prompts and responses are still logged for a limited period to detect abuse. The terms name no zero-retention option and no region list.

open_router.note: Zero retention is a per-request data policy that restricts the upstream pool, not a default, and the docs state the setting has no bearing on OpenRouter's own handling. The condition on this class is that the adapter honours the requirement per request: a request carrying the zero-retention requirement is sent with the deny data-collection policy, and the harness declares that through the zeroDataRetentionOnRequest feature, which is what admission reads. A request without the requirement sends nothing, so the pool narrows only for the organizations that asked.

vercel_gateway.note: Gateway's own layer only. Vercel states AI Gateway has a ZDR policy and does not retain prompts, outputs, or sensitive data, and that user data is immediately and permanently deleted after requests are completed; separately, AI Gateway does not use prompts or responses for training purposes (https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training). The paid team-wide or per-request zeroDataRetention toggle instead restricts routing to upstream model providers that have their own negotiated ZDR agreement with Vercel; that upstream policy varies by provider and applies per model, and is not covered by this record. No residency or region commitment is published for AI Gateway's own infrastructure.

cheaperinference.note: Gateway's own layer only, operated by Keak. Cheaper Inference does not store prompt or response bodies in its application database; request content is transmitted to the serving provider and temporary uploads expire after one hour (https://platform.cheaperinference.com/legal/dpa). Operational logs are retained up to 12 months, account and billing records for the agreement term plus seven years. Keak states it does not use customer prompt or response bodies to train Keak models. Upstream model providers may retain inputs under their own practices; that policy applies per model and is not covered here. Data may be processed in the United States, Canada, Europe, and other countries where Keak operates, no fixed residency list is published.

See the cheaperinference record for the sourced quotes; upstream model provider policy applies per model and is not covered here.

bedrock.note: Gateway's own layer (AWS), not the upstream model provider. Retention is set by a data_retention_mode the customer configures at account or project scope: none is zero data retention, no request or response data is written to durable storage by AWS or shared with the model provider; default applies the model's own retention behavior; aws_review and legacy provider_data_share retain content up to 30 days within the AWS boundary for AWS-performed human review some model providers require as a condition of access, content is never shared with the provider. Some models require aws_review as their minimum and do not permit none without a support-assisted eligibility process, contact your AWS account manager to discuss eligibility. AWS FAQ states AWS and third-party model providers will not use any inputs to or outputs from Amazon Bedrock to train Amazon Nova, Amazon Titan, or any third-party models (https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/faqs/). Bedrock is offered across many AWS regions the customer selects for inference; no fixed region list is recorded here. Upstream model provider policy still applies per model and is not covered by this record.

Also checked: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/about-nvidia/privacy-policy/ (retention section covers marketing and account engagement, not API data, no API-specific statement), https://build.nvidia.com/legal/privacy-policy (404), https://build.nvidia.com/docs/data-privacy (404), https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/data-privacy.html (404). groq.note: Groq's general privacy policy explicitly excludes GroqCloud, which is instead governed by the Groq Services Agreement and this Customer Data Processing Addendum. The DPA states data is retained for the time period needed to accomplish the purposes of processing unless applicable law requires longer, and that the customer may request deletion of personal data within a maximum period of 180 days. No dedicated zero-data-retention API feature is published, only this request-based deletion within up to 180 days, so this is recorded as unavailable rather than on_request. The DPA restricts processing to providing, maintaining and supporting the Cloud Services and to the customer's documented instructions, but does not explicitly state whether Groq trains models on customer data, so trainsOnInputs is left unknown. Personal data may be transferred to and processed in the United States and other countries where Groq or its subprocessors maintain processing operations, no fixed region list.

workers_ai.note: Workers AI runs open-weight models directly on Cloudflare's own infrastructure behind the AI Gateway compat endpoint; there is no separate third-party upstream provider layer for this route the way there is for vercel_gateway or bedrock. Cloudflare does not use customer content to train any AI models made available on Workers AI or to improve any Cloudflare or third-party services, and would not do so without explicit consent. AI Gateway request and response logs persist by default for an account-configured duration and can be turned off account-wide in dashboard settings, or per request via the cf-aig-collect-log:false header (drop all logging) or cf-aig-collect-log-payload:false (drop stored bodies, keep metadata) (https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/observability/logging/). No residency or region commitment is published for this route.

imageOutput.note: The provider's only active image family, so the slot's active model is the default by construction. Following the slot rather than naming a generation keeps a promotion from reaching this record.

Three active image families sit at the fast, balanced and best tiers. The balanced slot is the default: the fast tier trades quality a caller did not ask to give up, and the best tier costs twice as much per image. A caller wanting either names it explicitly.

Both aggregator routes can land on an image model. This one is the live route; the other is the preview and carries availability preview, so it is never the default. The key names no generation, so a catalog refresh does not reach this record.

Added the two OpenRouter router routes the product had no entry for: openrouter/auto (Auto Router) and openrouter/free (Free Models Router), and set open_router.defaultModel to openrouter/auto, which was previously empty so the provider had no route at all. Every field is read from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models retrieved 2026-08-29 with a live key. Auto Router: canonical_slug openrouter/auto, 2,000,000 context, tokenizer "Router", modality text+image+file+audio+video->text+image, and supported_parameters including reasoning, reasoning_effort, tools, tool_choice and structured_outputs, hence reasoning.control "effort". Free Models Router: canonical_slug openrouter/free, 200,000 context, modality text+image->text, pricing prompt "0" and completion "0", and supported_parameters including reasoning_effort, tools and structured_outputs. Both routes report pricing that is resolved per request, auto returns "-1" for prompt and completion because cost follows the model it selects, so no per-million rate is recorded here and reservation must price the resolved route, not the router. No benchmarks are recorded because OpenRouter publishes none for either router, and carrying a member model's numbers forward would be fabricated. openrouter/auto is recorded with inputCost/outputCost 0 because ModelMetadata requires both and the router publishes no rate of its own; managed metering must price the model the router actually resolved (the completion response reports it) rather than the router record, so this route is safe on BYOK, where OpenRouter bills the key holder directly, and must not be exposed on a metered managed plan until resolved-route pricing is wired. openrouter/free is genuinely zero-rated ("0"/"0" from the provider).

Both router routes were exercised end to end against the live API after the account key was rotated. openrouter/auto returned HTTP 200 in 752ms and reported routing to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, confirming the earlier note that the router itself publishes no rate and that metering must price the resolved model. openrouter/free returned HTTP 200 and routed to free members (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free, minimax/minimax-m2.7:free) with usage.cost 0, confirming the zero rating. Both free members are reasoning models whose reasoning tokens count against max_tokens: a 16-token cap returned empty content while a 200-token cap returned the expected text with finish_reason "stop" and 31 reasoning tokens. The product default is DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 8192, so this is not reachable in normal use, but any caller that lowers the cap for a free-router turn must leave room for reasoning tokens.

The recorded 4,000 was a video-model placeholder shared with the veo-3.1 rows and litellm's 131,072 matches nothing Google publishes. Prices on all three rows were re-read at the same time and are unchanged: gemini-3.1-pro-preview $2.00/$12.00 with $0.20 caching under 200k tokens and $4.00/$18.00/$0.40 above it; gemini-3.1-flash-image $0.50 input, $3.00 text output, $60.00 image output; gemini-omni-flash-preview $1.50 input, $9.00 text output, $17.50 video output. Sources retrieved 2026-09-01: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-flash-image, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-omni-flash.

DeepSeek publishes a peak/off-peak rate card, and both V4 rows carried figures that match neither half of it. Peak is $0.44/$1.32 per 1M with a $0.014 cache hit for deepseek-v4-flash and $1.32/$3.96 with a $0.044 cache hit for deepseek-v4-pro; off-peak is exactly half of each, and peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Monday through Friday. Both rows now carry the peak rate as a curation costOverride, because peak is the only figure never undercut on any date and the schema has no field for a time-of-day split; the same reasoning moved providers.deepseek.defaultPricing, the cost-calculator fallback for unrecognised deepseek ids, from $0.14/$0.28 to $0.44/$1.32. The prior values ($0.14/$0.28/$0.0028 for flash, $0.435/$0.87/$0.003625 for pro) came from models.dev, which still publishes them for the first-party deepseek provider; litellm's first-party deepseek entry independently agrees with the peak rate. The pro row additionally asserted that DeepSeek made a 75% launch discount permanent on 2026-05-22, no discount, promotion or expiry language appears anywhere on DeepSeek's pricing page, so that claim is withdrawn. The override lives in curation rather than the synced snapshot so a later models.dev refresh cannot silently restore the undercharge. gpt-image-2 was checked in the same pass and is correct as recorded: OpenAI publishes an image row at $8.00 input, $2.00 cached input, $30.00 output and a separate text row at $5.00 input, $1.25 cached input, and this entry carries the image row throughout, so the $2.00 cache read stands and the $1.25 a snapshot reports is the text row. Sources retrieved 2026-09-01: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.
